# ABSTRACT {#abstract .unnumbered .unlisted}

Accurate Domestic Value Added Tax (VAT) forecasts are essential for budgeting and fiscal planning in Ghana. In 2024, Domestic VAT fell 24.3% short of its target although total tax revenue exceeded its target, and, to the best of our knowledge, no earlier study had applied machine learning to Domestic VAT forecasting in Ghana. This study applied four machine learning models, namely the Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO), Support Vector Regression (SVR), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) and a one-dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (1D-CNN), to forecast monthly Domestic VAT revenue and compared them with Naive, Seasonal Naive and ARIMAX benchmarks. The data were 192 monthly observations from January 2010 to December 2025 on Domestic VAT, the exchange rate, the Treasury bill rate, the Composite Index of Economic Activity (CIEA) and inflation. Every model forecast the monthly change in log VAT from 15 predictors built from earlier months only. The models were tuned by rolling validation on data up to December 2023 and tested on the last 24 months using RMSE, MAE and MAPE. SVR was the most accurate model on all three measures (RMSE 201.40, MAE 145.59, MAPE 9.36%), but its lead over ARIMAX (RMSE 201.94, MAPE 9.52%) was very small. LASSO and XGBoost beat the Naive forecast but not ARIMAX, the 1D-CNN did no better than the Naive forecast, and all models missed a sharp jump in August 2024. Past VAT changes, the previous month’s changes in economic activity and the exchange rate, and the December effect were the main drivers of VAT growth. Machine learning therefore matched, and slightly improved on, ARIMAX, but with fewer than 200 observations the gains were small. The study recommended that the Ghana Revenue Authority use SVR together with ARIMAX for one-month-ahead forecasts and record policy and administrative events.

**Keywords:** Domestic VAT; revenue forecasting; machine learning; support vector regression; ARIMAX; Ghana
